findings.description: The bucket sets no ACL and has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and the inline comment states it is public; the customer-master.xlsx object stored in it would therefore be readable by anonymous internet users.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so customer master data in this bucket is stored without SSE-KMS encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to this public bucket holding customer data leaves no audit trail for detection or forensics.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy = true, so objects can be silently overwritten or destroyed with no recovery path or tamper evidence.
customer-master.xlsx, apparently a customer PII dataset, is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data which is public and unencrypted, and no kms_key_id is set on the object itself.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket holding financial records, leaving them unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to financial data is not auditable.
Versioning is disabled and force_destroy is true, so financial objects can be overwritten or destroyed with no recovery or tamper evidence.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose financial data publicly without a guardrail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so operations data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so reads and writes to this bucket are not recorded for audit or incident response.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving no guardrail against future public ACLs or bucket policies.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so data science datasets are stored unencrypted while the logs bucket in the same file correctly uses SSE-KMS.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving no guardrail against accidental public exposure.
The log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; access logs reveal internal access patterns and identities if an ACL or policy later exposes them.
The audit-log destination bucket has no object lock or MFA delete and sets force_destroy = true, allowing an attacker with credentials to destroy the audit trail.
No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false on any bucket in this file, including the KMS-encrypted logs bucket, so data may be transmitted over plaintext HTTP.
